Exceptional Gold Intercepts Across Multiple Vein Systems at the Blueberry Contact Zone

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Scottie Resources Corp. (TSXV: SCOT) (OTCQB: SCTSF) (FSE: SR80) ("Scottie" or the "Company") is pleased to report additional high-grade gold intercepts from its 2026 drilling at the Blueberry Contact Zone within the Scottie Gold Mine Project. The road-accessible Scottie Gold Mine Project, which includes the 100% owned historic mine and adjacent Blueberry Contact Zone, is located 35 kilometres north of Stewart, British Columbia.

This latest batch of 2026 drill results delivers significant high-grade gold intercepts across the Blueberry, Fifi and Lemoffe vein systems reinforcing grade and continuity of the established mineralisation. This support the potential conversion of Inferred to Indicated resources, while a separate high-grade intercept below the modelled Blueberry 5 vein highlights the potential for additional mineralised structures. High-grade intercepts at Fifi and Lemoffe, including several beyond the existing PEA stope outlines, further demonstrate opportunities for resource growth and potential expansion of the PEA mine design.

The 2026 drilling program at the Scottie Gold Mine Project has concluded, with 61,578 metres ("m") drilled across 227 holes and assay results for the majority of holes still outstanding. Results from the program will inform the Company's updated Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") and Feasibility Study, both targeted for the first half of 2027. Figures 1-5 illustrate the reported drilling relative to the modelled vein zones.

Investors are encouraged to visit our website www.scottieresources.com to view the interactive 3D model showing the distribution of these released holes relative to modeled geology and prior drilling results.

Highlights

  • Exceptional high-grade infill results at Blueberry 3 and 4: Hole SR26-560 returned 25.5 grams per tonne (g/t) gold over 14.00 metres (m), including 17.6 g/t gold over 8.00 m at Blueberry 3 (including 29.5 g/t gold over 4.50 m) and 72.1 g/t gold over 3.00 m at Blueberry 4. Located about 20 m beyond the existing PEA stope outline, this intercept reinforces the strength of the established mineralised system while highlighting the potential to expand the mineable envelope beyond the current PEA design (Table 1, Figures 1 and 2).

  • High-grade gold intercept beyond existing vein models: Hole SR26-522 intersected 120.0 g/t gold over 1.50 m, approximately 20 m below the modelled Blueberry 5 vein, highlighting the potential for additional high-grade mineralisation beyond the currently modelled veins (Table 1, Figure 1).

  • High-grade mineralisation continues at Fifi: Hole SR26-563 intersected 10.1 g/t gold over 11.00 m, including 50.1 g/t gold over 2.00 m, in the upper portion of Fifi 1, approximately 40 m beyond the 2025 PEA stope outline. At Fifi 2, hole SR26-540 returned 5.8 g/t gold over 6.85 m, including 33.0 g/t gold over 1.00 m, approximately 30 m outboard of the existing PEA stope outline. Additional intercepts of 6.2 g/t gold over 4.00 m at Fifi 3 (SR26-563) and 8.3 g/t gold over 2.50 m at Fifi 2 (SR26-560) reinforce the potential to expand the existing resource across the Fifi vein system (Table 1, Figures 1, 3 and 4).

  • Drilling reinforces high-grade mineralisation at Lemoffe 4: Hole SR26-525 intersected 8.5 g/t gold over 3.75 m just outside the existing resource and 2025 PEA stope outline, as well as 11.7 g/t gold over 1.35 m approximately 10 m below the modelled vein. Additional results include 3.9 g/t gold over 5.90 m, including 15.2 g/t gold over 1.35 m in SR26-564, outside the existing resource blocks, while SR26-559 and SR26-565 returned 5.4 g/t gold over 4.65 m and 2.7 g/t gold over 7.00 m, respectively, within the current PEA mine design. These results reinforce grade and continuity within the established Lemoffe 4 system while highlighting potential additions beyond the existing resource and mine plan (Table 1, Figures 1 and 5).

"The results we're seeing from the Blueberry Contact Zone continue to impress, and this latest round of drilling is no exception," commented Dr. Thomas Mumford, President and CEO of Scottie Resources. "We're not only reinforcing the strength of the existing resource, but also identifying high-grade mineralisation that could meaningfully enhance the current PEA mine design. As we move toward our updated Mineral Resource Estimate and Feasibility Study, we believe these results will further augment an already compelling project."

Quality Assurance and Control

Results from samples taken during the 2026 field season were analyzed at SGS Minerals in Burnaby, BC. The sampling program is undertaken under the direction of Lyle Hansen. The majority of drill core is NQ in diameter, with select holes of HQ size primarily taken for geomechanical purposes. Prior to sampling drill core is cut in half lengthwise, with half sent for assay and the remaining half kept in Stewart, BC. Standards, blanks, and duplicate samples were taken at intervals and frequencies that meet or exceed industry best practices. A secure chain of custody is maintained in transporting and storing all samples. Gold is assayed using a fire assay with atomic absorption spectrometry and gravimetric finish when required (+9 g/t gold). Analysis by four acid digestion with multi-element ICP-AES analysis is conducted on all samples with silver and base metal over-limits being re-analyzed by emission spectrometry.

Lyle Hansen, P.Geo., Resource Geologist for Scottie Resources Corp., is non-independent and a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects and has reviewed and approved the scientific and technical information contained in this news release.

ABOUT SCOTTIE RESOURCES CORP.

Scottie Resources holds 100% interest in the Scottie Gold Mine Property, which includes the high-grade, past-producing Scottie Gold Mine and the adjacent Blueberry Contact Zone. The Company also owns a 100% interest in the Georgia Project, host to the past-producing Georgia River Mine, as well as the Cambria, Sulu, and Tide North properties. In total, Scottie controls approximately 58,500 hectares of highly prospective mineral claims within the Stewart Mining Camp in British Columbia's Golden Triangle—one of the world's most prolific mineralised districts.

Scottie's current resource estimate on the Scottie Gold Mine Project includes a total of 703,000 gold ounces at an average grade of 6.1 g/t (Inferred category) in 3.6 million tonnes, highlighting the development potential for a significant near-surface, high-grade deposit. The Company's strategy is to continue expanding this resource and to define additional mineralisation around past-producing mines through systematic drilling and surface exploration.

The Company has recently completed a PEA for the Scottie Gold Mine (Bird et al., October 28, 2025, Scottie Gold Mine Project, SEDAR+). The PEA outlines a robust ore sorting and Direct-Ship Ore (DSO) development scenario with strong economics and significant upside through a potential toll-milling option utilizing excess capacity at the nearby Premier mill. The base case DSO project delivers an after-tax NPV(5%) of $215.8-$668.3 million at gold prices of US$2,600-$4,200/oz, respectively. Under the toll-milling scenario, project economics improve substantially, with an after-tax NPV(5%) of $380-$832 million (no agreement currently in place). The PEA estimates initial capital costs of $129 million, average annual production of ~65,400 oz gold over seven years, and a payback period of 1.7 years for the after-tax DSO case—reduced to just 0.9 years under the toll-milling opportunity at US$2,600/oz.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Tartisan Nickel Corp. (CSE: TN) (OTCQB: TTSRF) (FSE: 8TA) ("Tartisan" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that its wholly owned subsidiary, Canadian Arrow Mines Limited, has received Early Exploration Permit PR-26-000146 for the Turtle Pond Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project, approximately 40 kilometres south of Dryden in Northwestern Ontario. The Ontario Ministry of Energy and Mines issued the three-year permit on November 17, 2026.

Turtle Pond is located approximately 70 kilometres east of Tartisan's Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project near Sioux Narrows. The two properties form part of the Company's regional critical minerals portfolio. As exploration advances, Tartisan intends to assess opportunities for future operational synergies between the projects.

Proposed Exploration Program

The proposed program comprises 14 diamond drill holes totalling approximately 2,880 metres in two phases. The first phase consists of six holes totalling approximately 1,060 metres at the Double E, Night Danger and Glatz showings. These holes are designed to twin selected historical holes, evaluate historical results and geological relationships, and provide fresh core for potential metallurgical testing.

The second phase comprises eight holes totalling approximately 1,820 metres to test electromagnetic conductors, magnetic anomalies and interpreted extensions of known mineralization. Targets are informed by ground electromagnetic and airborne geophysical surveys completed in 2024 and 2025.

Supporting work includes geological mapping, surface sampling, Beep Mat surveying and brushing of existing access trails, with surface exploration focused in part on the approximately 1.5-kilometre corridor between North Glatz and Emmons Lake. Final drill locations, sequencing and metres will be refined as field information becomes available. The proposed work remains subject to financing, contractor availability, permit conditions and any additional authorizations required.

"The Turtle Pond permit allows us to advance planning for a program that will revisit the Double E, Night Danger and Glatz showings and test additional geophysical targets," said Mark Appleby, President and CEO of Tartisan. "Turtle Pond's proximity to Kenbridge adds to its strategic interest within our Ontario portfolio. Our objective is to build a clearer understanding of its nickel-copper-cobalt potential through systematic exploration."

About the Turtle Pond Project

Turtle Pond comprises 165 contiguous claim units covering approximately 3,454 hectares in the Turtlepond Lake and Ukik Lake areas of the Kenora Mining District. The property is held through Canadian Arrow Mines Limited and is accessible from Highway 502 by existing logging roads and trails.

Nickel-copper-cobalt sulphide mineralization, with associated platinum and palladium reported at Double E, occurs in mafic and ultramafic intrusive rocks within the Wabigoon Subprovince of the Archean Superior Province. Further drilling is required to evaluate the extent and continuity of mineralization.

Community Engagement and Environmental Stewardship

Tartisan is committed to ongoing engagement with First Nations and Indigenous communities as exploration planning advances. Work at Turtle Pond will follow the permit's terms, including advance notification and seasonal restrictions, as well as applicable early exploration standards and rehabilitation requirements.

Qualified Person

Dean MacEachern, P.Geo., an independent consultant to the Company and a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101, has reviewed and approved the technical content of this news release.

Tartisan Nickel Corp. is a Canadian-based critical minerals exploration and development company whose assets include the Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project near Sioux Narrows in Northwestern Ontario, the Sill Lake Silver-Lead-Zinc Project near Sault Ste. Marie, and the Turtle Pond Project near Dryden, Ontario.

Tartisan's common shares are listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (CSE: TN), OTCQB (TTSRF) and Frankfurt Stock Exchange (8TA). Currently, there are 158,195,904 shares issued and outstanding (160,916,961 fully diluted). Vancouver, Canada, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Clearmind Medicine Inc. (Nasdaq: CMND) (“Clearmind” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing non-hallucinogenic psychedelic-derived neuroplastogens for scalable treatment of neuropsychiatric, metabolic, and addiction disorders including Alcohol Use Disorder (“AUD”), today announced the publication of a Hong Kong patent application covering innovative psychedelic compounds targeting the treatment of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (“PTSD”) and other mental health disorders.

The patent application is part of the Company's exclusive worldwide licensing agreement with Yissum Research Development Company of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (“Yissum”). The compounds were invented by Professors Ahmed Masaewa, Rami Yaka, and Avi Priel of the Hebrew University. Under the licensing agreement, Clearmind holds exclusive global rights to develop, manufacture, and commercialize the novel compounds.

The Hong Kong patent publication expands Clearmind's global patent application portfolio for its proprietary PTSD-focused psychedelic compounds. Together with existing international filings, the application supports the Company's strategy to seek intellectual property protection for its novel therapeutic candidates across major global markets.

According to market research by Heimdall Insights, the global PTSD therapeutics market was valued at approximately $19 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $24.8 billion by 2030, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 5.5%. In addition, GlobalData projects that the PTSD pharmaceutical market across seven major markets is projected to grow from $1.2 billion in 2024 to $5.5 billion by 2034, at a CAGR of 16.1%,  reflecting anticipated demand for innovative treatment options.

About Clearmind Medicine Inc.

Clearmind is a clinical-stage neuroplastogens pharmaceutical biotech company focused on the discovery and development of non-hallucinogenic, second generation, neuroplastogen-derived therapeutics to solve widespread and underserved health problems, including alcohol use disorder. Its primary objective is to research and develop psychedelic-based compounds and attempt to commercialize them as regulated medicines, foods, or supplements.

The Company’s intellectual property portfolio currently consists of nineteen patent families, including 32 granted patents. The Company intends to seek additional patents for its compounds whenever warranted and will remain opportunistic regarding the acquisition of additional intellectual property to build its portfolio.

Shares of Clearmind are listed for trading on Nasdaq under the symbol "CMND."

TEL AVIV, Israel, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Arbe Robotics Ltd. (NASDAQ: ARBE) (TASE: ARBE), a global leader in ultra-high-resolution radar solutions, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Recent Highlights

  • Level 3 automotive program win: One of the world's largest automotive groups selected Hirain's imaging radar, powered by Arbe's chipset, for a Level 3 passenger vehicle program across multiple brands in China. Series-production radar deliveries are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027, putting Arbe on a defined path to automotive mass production.
  • Defense program advances to orders and deliveries: During the quarter, a leading global defense and homeland security system integrator selected Arbe for three civilian and defense projects under a framework agreement. Since the announcement, Arbe has received initial orders and delivered radar systems.
  • Alerion counter-drone radar launched: Arbe introduced Alerion, an ultra-high-resolution counter-drone radar, designed to detect small, low-flying threats, including hard-to-detect autonomous and fiber-optic drones. Alerion has been field-tested and is built to protect critical infrastructure and defense assets. As the threat continues to escalate, industry analysts expect significant growth in the global counter-UAS (Unmanned Aircraft Systems) market over the coming years.
  • Early defense momentum: Shortly after entering the defense market, Arbe is already seeing commercial engagement. Beyond the projects with the global system integrator described above, Arbe has initiated two additional integration projects addressing immediate customer needs and is in early-stage evaluations for more than eight projects.
  • Off road autonomy: During the quarter, Arbe's Tier 1, Sensrad, announced a collaboration with VirtuRail to integrate its radar system, based on Arbe's chipset, into automated tunnel construction vehicles operating in dust, smoke and darkness.
  • $15 million capital raise: Arbe closed a $15 million underwritten registered direct offering led by two leading US institutional investors, including AWM's Special Situations Funds, one of the major shareholders of Arbe. Together with a reduced quarterly cash burn, the proceeds strengthen Arbe's financial position and support scaling for its Level 3 automotive program, expansion into the defense segment and other growth initiatives.
  • New Chief Financial Officer: Arbe appointed Assaf Pereg, CPA, as Chief Financial Officer, effective August 30, 2026. He brings Arbe nearly 20 years of financial leadership experience in both US-listed public technology companies and start-ups.

Management Comments

Ram Machness, CEO of Arbe, commented, "The third quarter was a turning point for Arbe. Our Level 3 program win with one of the world's largest automotive groups validates years of development and testing and puts us on the path to automotive mass production. Furthermore, our $15 million capital raise, led by institutional investors, shows continued trust in our ongoing strategic plan."

"Building on our leading chipset technology, we are expanding our radar system portfolio beyond automotive, a key strategic step that opens new markets for us. Alongside Phoenix, our automotive radar system, this quarter we launched Alerion, our counter-drone radar. Alerion finds small, low-flying drones, including autonomous and fiber-optic drones that are hard for other sensors to detect. This strategy is already showing early results: a leading global system integrator selected us for three projects, and we have received orders and delivered systems, with more integration projects already underway. Defense and counter-drone programs have shorter sales cycles, and they are additive and complement our long-term automotive business. Our focus now is on turning customer interest into revenue."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Highlights

Revenues for Q3 2026 were $0.8 million, compared to $0.3 million in Q3 2025.

Gross profit for Q3 2026 was approximately break-even, compared to a gross loss of $0.2 million in Q3 2025.

Operating expenses in Q3 2026 were $9.1 million, compared to $11.3 million in Q3 2025.

The lower expenses were primarily driven by lower share-based compensation expenses and lower labor costs paid this quarter, compared to Q3 2025. Operating loss in Q3 2026 was $9.1 million, compared to an $11.5 million loss in Q3 2025.

Net loss in Q3 2026 decreased to $9.0 million, compared to a net loss of $11.0 million in Q3 2025.

Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026, a non-GAAP measure that excludes expenses for non-cash share-based compensation and non-recurring items, improved to a loss of $8.0 million, compared with a loss of $9.2 million in Q3 2025.

Management believes that this non-GAAP measurement is important in evaluating our use of cash and in planning our cash requirements in the coming period.

Balance Sheet and Liquidity Highlights

As of September 30, 2026, Arbe had $48.0 million in cash, cash equivalents, long-term and short-term bank deposits. These include the $13.8 million net proceeds of the offering completed in September 2026.

As of September 30, 2026, Arbe had $46.3 million in shareholders' equity.

The Company remains in compliance with the financial covenants set forth in the convertible debentures and holds cash substantially above the minimum threshold.

Outlook

Arbe is updating its full-year 2026 outlook provided in February 2026.

Based on current market conditions and customer engagement visibility, the Company's outlook for 2026 is as follows:

  • Revenue in the range of $2.3 million to $3.0 million. The revised range reflects the timing of two integration projects, for which deliveries and related revenue recognition were originally expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and have shifted to 2027.
  • Adjusted EBITDA for 2026 is projected to be a loss in the range of $34 million to $35 million. The revised range reflects lower expected revenue for 2026 and the Company's strategic investment in building a production line for radar systems and in building inventory to position the Company for potential order growth in the coming year.

This outlook reflects management's current expectations as of today and is subject to change based on market conditions, customer adoption timelines, and other factors.

Company advances its internally developed drug discovery program targeting acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) and AgPlenus' fungicide discovery programs targeting novel MoA against Septoria

REHOVOT, Israel, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evogene Ltd. (Nasdaq: EVGN) (TASE: EVGN), a computational chemistry company leveraging proprietary AI-driven technologies to design and develop novel small molecules for the pharmaceutical and agricultural industries, today reported its financial results for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, and provided an update on its business activities.

Ofer Haviv, Evogene's President and CEO, stated: "During the third quarter, we continued to advance our strategy of leveraging our proprietary AI-driven discovery platform, ChemPass AI™, to develop innovative small-molecule-based products with significant commercial potential. Alongside our collaborative discovery activities, we are advancing two internal development programs that represent an important component of our strategy to build a pipeline of proprietary assets fully owned and managed by Evogene.

The first one is our internal drug discovery program targeting acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD), a serious medical condition associated with significant unmet medical need. Within just several months, Using ChemPass AI™, we generated a series of novel, small-molecule candidates, that demonstrated biological potency, at nanomolar concentrations, as well as encouraging preliminary ADME and toxicology profiles. We are now focused on further optimizing these molecules, identifying the most promising candidates, and advancing the program toward IND-enabling studies. (For more information, please see our PR from 28, October 2026)

The second program, conducted through our subsidiary AgPlenus, focuses on discovering fungicides with new modes of action targeting Septoria tritici blotch, a major wheat disease for which resistance to existing fungicides is a growing challenge. Using ChemPass AI for Ag™, AgPlenus identified compounds that showed promising activity against fungicide-resistant Septoria strains. Selected compounds also reduced disease severity by up to 75%, compared to untreated controls, in plant tissue assays and demonstrating activity against additional fungal pathogens, indicating broader fungicidal potential. (For more information, please see our PR from 17, November 2026)

The progresses achieved across these initiatives demonstrates the ability of ChemPass AI™ and ChemPass AI for Ag™ to translate computational discovery into experimentally validated molecules exhibiting promising biological activity. More importantly, these programs reflect our strategic focus on converting technological capabilities into differentiated, proprietary product candidates offering meaningful commercial potential, ultimately creating long-term value for Evogene and its shareholders. "

Financial Results and Analysis

Cash Position

As of September 30, 2026, Evogene held consolidated cash, cash equivalents and short-term bank deposits of approximately $9.2 million. Consolidated cash usage during the third quarter of 2026 was approximately $2.4 million, including a Directors' and Officers' insurance payment of approximately $0.5 million, covering an 18-month period.

Revenues

Revenues for the nine months of 2026 totaled approximately $0.8 million, compared to approximately $3.2 million in the same period of 2025, representing a decrease of approximately $2.4 million. The decrease is mainly attributable to lower revenue recognized by Casterra, which in the first half of 2025 included significant seed sales of approximately $2.0 million. Revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were approximately $0.1 million compared to approximately $0.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, mainly due to the conclusion of the license and collaboration agreement with Bayer in May 2026.

Research and Development Expenses

Research and development expenses, net of non-refundable grants, for the nine months of 2026 were approximately $4.5 million, compared to approximately $4.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025, representing a decrease of approximately $0.1 million. For the third quarter of 2026, R&D expenses were approximately $1.5 million, an increase from $1.1 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was mainly attributable to the recognition of a non-refundable grant of approximately $0.2 million and an adjustment to liabilities in respect of government grants of approximately $0.1 million, both of which reduced R&D expenses in the third quarter of 2025, as well as the impact of fluctuations in the USD/NIS exchange rate, between the periods.

Sales and Marketing Expenses

Sales and marketing expenses for the nine months of 2026 were approximately $0.9 million, compared to approximately $1.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025. Sales and marketing expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were approximately $0.2 million, compared to approximately $0.4 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to lower sales and marketing expenses at Casterra and AgPlenus.

General and Administrative Expenses

General and administrative expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, decreased slightly to approximately $3.1 million, compared to approximately $3.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, general and administrative expenses were approximately $1.1 million, remaining relatively unchanged compared to the same period of 2025. The decrease in general and administrative expenses across Evogene and its subsidiaries was largely offset, mainly by transaction costs associated with the warrant inducement transaction and additional non-recurring legal expenses related to corporate governance and shareholders matters. These costs totaled approximately $0.4 million and $0.3 million during the nine-month and three-month periods ended September 30, 2026, respectively.

Financing Expenses (Income), Net

Financing expenses, net, for the nine months of 2026 were approximately $1.6 million, compared to financing income, net, of approximately $0.9 million in the corresponding period of 2025. This change was primarily related to the accounting treatment and revaluation of warrants, including warrants issued in the August 2024 financing and the February 2026 warrant inducement transaction. As part of the February 2026 warrant inducement transaction, the Company recorded financing expenses of approximately $3.8 million during the first nine months of 2026. In addition, the Company recorded financing income of approximately $2.3 million related to the revaluation of warrants liability as of September 30, 2026. For the third quarter of 2026, financing income, net, was approximately $176 thousand, compared to approximately $79 thousand in the corresponding period of 2025, with no material change between the periods.

Loss from Discontinued Operations

Loss from discontinued operations, net, for the nine months of 2026 was approximately $0.5 million, compared to an income from discontinued operations, net, of approximately $4.0 million in the corresponding period of 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, the loss from discontinued operations was approximately $0.06 million, compared to income of approximately $7.6 million in the third quarter of the previous year. These amounts primarily reflect the financial results of Lavie Bio's and Biomica's operations, as well as expenses related to the development and maintenance of MicroBoost AI for Ag, which are presented as a single-line item in the consolidated statements of profit and loss. Following the sale of the majority of Lavie Bio's assets, as well as Evogene's MicroBoost AI for Ag, to ICL in July 2025 and the licensing agreement with Lishan in February 2026, Lavie Bio's and Biomica's operating expense levels have decreased significantly. Biomica's operations were classified as discontinued operations beginning in the second quarter of 2026, and accordingly, the 2025 comparative figures have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. Lavie Bio's operations, as well as expenses related to the development and maintenance of MicroBoost AI for Ag, had already been classified as discontinued operations in 2025.

Net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was approximately $10.5 million, compared to approximately $2.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025. The $8.0 million increase in net loss was primarily attributable to lower revenues, higher financing expenses, and income recognized in connection with the ICL transaction during the corresponding period of 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, net loss was approximately $2.9 million, compared to net income of approximately $5.2 million in the same period of 2025. The change was primarily attributable to income recognized in connection with the ICL transaction during the third quarter of 2025, as discussed above.

About Evogene Ltd.

Evogene Ltd. (NASDAQ: EVGN) (TASE: EVGN) is a pioneering company in computational chemistry, specializing in the generative design of small molecules for drug development and ag chemical products. At the core of its technology is ChemPass AITM, a proprietary generative AI designed to explore vast chemical space and generate novel, highly potent small molecules optimized across multiple critical parameters. Built on this powerful technological foundation, and through strategic partnerships alongside internal product development, Evogene is focused on creating breakthrough products for the pharmaceutical and agricultural industries, driven by the integration of scientific innovation with real-world industry needs.

For more information, please visit www.evogene.com. 

About AgPlenus Ltd. 

AgPlenus, a subsidiary of Evogene Ltd., is an AI-driven crop protection discovery company focused on developing effective and sustainable solutions to address the growing challenge of pesticide resistance. The company leverages ChemPass AI for Ag™, a technology platform licensed from Evogene, integrating predictive biology, artificial intelligence, and computational chemistry to discover novel crop-protection molecules. Through its target-based discovery approach, AgPlenus aims to improve discovery efficiency, reduce development risks, and advance differentiated crop-protection solutions with the potential to address unmet agricultural needs. 

For more information, please visit www.agplenus.com

KIO-401 has been evaluated in Phase 2 and Phase 3 CRAO studies in Japan. Building on those studies, Kiora plans to initiate a multinational Phase 3 registration trial in CRAO in 2027. The company also plans to evaluate KIO-401 in a Phase 2b trial in non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).

The video interview will be available for 90 days in the Events section of Kiora’s investor relations website.

About Kiora

Kiora Pharmaceuticals is a late-stage retinal therapeutics company developing small-molecule therapies targeting differentiated biological pathways implicated in vision-threatening diseases.

KIO-401 is an oral, neuroprotective calpain inhibitor in development for central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) and non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), two rare, acute ischemic ophthalmic diseases with no approved pharmacologic treatments. Kiora is planning a multinational Phase 3 registration trial in CRAO and a Phase 2b clinical trial in NAION. The KIO-401 platform also has potential applications in additional ophthalmic indications, including glaucoma, where calpain-mediated injury may contribute to disease progression.

KIO-301 is a partnered Phase 2 photoswitch therapy for advanced retinitis pigmentosa. KIO-104, a DHODH inhibitor previously evaluated in the KLARITY clinical trial for retinal inflammation and fibrosis, is available for partnering or out-licensing.

Integration will bring three Canadian-hosted AI models to Railtown's Conductr platform and AI Partner Marketplace, combining Canadian AI inference with Railtown's agent development, knowledge infrastructure and deployment technologies.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Railtown AI Technologies Inc. (CSE: RAIL) (OTCQB: RLAIF) ("Railtown" or the "Company") is pleased to announce a Technology Integration Partnership with Radium, a frontier model alternative with drop-in LLM APIs to replace OpenAI and Anthropic. Radium's models, Hal, Clarke and Tycho, are available with hosting in Canada.

Under the partnership, Railtown and Radium are working to integrate three of Radium's AI models directly into Railtown's Conductr platform, making them accessible to Railtown customers and participating technology partners within the AI Partner Marketplace.

The integration is intended to provide developers and organizations with additional model choices while supporting growing demand for AI solutions that prioritize Canadian data residency, security and operational control.

By combining Radium's Canadian-hosted AI models with Railtown's Conductr, Railengine and Railtracks technologies, the companies aim to provide a comprehensive technology foundation for building, deploying and managing intelligent AI applications and agents.

Addressing the Growing Demand for Sovereign AI

As artificial intelligence adoption accelerates across Canadian businesses and institutions, data sovereignty is becoming an increasingly important consideration in technology procurement and deployment decisions.

Organizations operating in industries such as financial services, healthcare, government and professional services must consider where sensitive information is stored, processed and accessed when evaluating AI solutions.

While many organizations are eager to adopt AI-powered applications, concerns surrounding data residency, privacy, security and reliance on foreign-hosted infrastructure can create barriers to implementation.

The Railtown and Radium partnership is designed to help address these requirements by combining Canadian-hosted AI model inference with the development, knowledge management, deployment and observability capabilities available through Railtown's technology ecosystem.

Radium's Canadian hosting options provide an important component of this approach, while Railtown's technology enables developers and organizations to build and operate applications around those models.

Together, the companies intend to provide customers with greater flexibility in designing AI solutions that align with their data-residency and operational requirements.

Three Radium AI Models to Be Integrated into Conductr

The integration will introduce three Radium models into Railtown's Conductr platform, providing developers with options for selecting AI models based on application requirements, performance characteristics and workload complexity.

Hal - Advanced Reasoning and Agent Workflows

Designed for complex reasoning, coding, tool execution and sophisticated multi-step agent workflows.

Clarke - Enterprise Knowledge and Conversational AI

Designed for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), knowledge-based applications, conversational AI and enterprise information retrieval.

Tycho - High-Efficiency AI Processing

Designed for high-volume workloads, including document classification, information extraction and other applications where processing efficiency is important.

Through Conductr, customers will be able to select Radium models as part of their agent development and deployment workflows, subject to completion of the integration.

This approach supports Railtown's broader strategy of providing developers with access to multiple AI models and infrastructure providers through a unified technology platform.

Combining Canadian-Hosted AI Models with Railtown's Technology Ecosystem

Railtown's technology platform is designed to support the lifecycle of intelligent applications and AI agents. Refer to News Release dated October 15th, 2026, for description of commercialization.

Its core technologies include:

  • Conductr: Railtown's agentic AI orchestration, deployment and observability platform, providing developers and organizations with capabilities to deploy, manage, monitor and evaluate AI agents.
  • Railengine: Railtown's knowledge and data infrastructure, enabling AI applications and agents to access relevant enterprise information and persistent knowledge bases.
  • Railtracks: Railtown's open-source Agent Development Kit, providing developers with frameworks for creating specialized AI agents and intelligent workflows.

The addition of Radium's Canadian-hosted models is intended to complement these capabilities by providing model inference options for organizations seeking Canadian data residency.

For customers requiring a sovereign AI architecture, the combined technologies can support solutions in which model inference, enterprise knowledge and agent workloads are configured to operate within approved Canadian infrastructure environments.

The resulting architecture is intended to give customers greater control over their AI technology choices while simplifying the development and management of production AI applications.

Extending Sovereign AI Capabilities Through Canadian Data Centre Partnerships

Beyond providing access to Canadian-hosted AI models, Railtown is pursuing a broader strategy of working with Canadian cloud and data centre infrastructure providers to support sovereign AI deployments.

Through these relationships, Railtown aims to combine its Conductr, Railengine and Railtracks technologies with Canadian-hosted computing infrastructure, enabling organizations to build, deploy and manage intelligent applications while maintaining greater control over where their enterprise data, knowledge bases and AI workloads reside.

The integration of Radium's Canadian-hosted models represents an important complementary component of this strategy.

While Radium provides Canadian-based AI model inference, Railtown's technology ecosystem provides the software infrastructure required to connect enterprise knowledge, develop specialized AI agents, orchestrate intelligent workflows and monitor their execution.

By bringing these capabilities together with Canadian data centre infrastructure, Railtown intends to support more comprehensive sovereign AI architectures in which model inference, enterprise knowledge and agent execution can be configured to operate within Canadian hosting environments.

This approach is particularly relevant for Canadian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), government organizations and businesses operating in regulated industries that want to adopt artificial intelligence while addressing data residency, privacy and security requirements.

Railtown believes that combining Canadian-hosted AI models, Canadian infrastructure providers and its proprietary software technologies will help reduce the complexity of deploying sovereign AI solutions and provide Canadian organizations with a more accessible path to adopting production-ready agentic applications.

Importantly, this strategy also provides Railtown with opportunities to expand its commercial relationships with infrastructure providers, technology integration partners and customers seeking Canadian-hosted AI solutions.

Management Commentary

Cory Brandolini, Chief Executive Officer of Railtown AI, commented:

"One of the most important developments we are seeing in the Canadian AI market is the growing demand for sovereign AI solutions. Canadian organizations increasingly want the benefits of artificial intelligence, but they also want greater control over where their data resides, where their applications operate and how their AI infrastructure is managed.

"We have been working closely with the Radium team over the last several quarters, testing their models and APIs, and our development team has been extremely impressed with both the quality of their technology and the capabilities of their models. Radium has built an impressive AI offering, and we believe their Canadian-hosted models are a natural complement to Railtown's technology ecosystem.

"What makes this partnership particularly compelling is the combination of our respective technologies. Radium provides the AI models and Canadian hosting capabilities, while Railtown provides the tools and infrastructure developers need to build, connect, deploy and observe intelligent applications. Together, we believe we can help Canadian businesses move beyond experimenting with AI toward implementing practical, production-ready solutions that address their operational and data-residency requirements.

"Our strategy extends beyond integrating AI models. We are actively building relationships with Canadian data centre and cloud infrastructure providers to create a broader ecosystem for sovereign AI deployment. When you combine Canadian-hosted models from Radium with Railtown's agent development, knowledge infrastructure, deployment and observability technologies, and the ability to run critical workloads within Canadian data centres, we believe you have the foundation for a compelling end-to-end sovereign AI solution. This is particularly important for Canadian SMEs that want to adopt AI but may not have the internal technical resources to assemble and manage these technologies themselves.

"We also see an important commercial opportunity through our AI Partner Marketplace. By making Radium's models available to our growing network of technology partners, we can provide those companies with additional tools to develop and deliver sovereign AI solutions to their own customers. We believe this creates opportunities for both companies while strengthening Railtown's position within Canada's emerging sovereign AI ecosystem."

Expanding Opportunities Through the AI Partner Marketplace

The Radium integration is also expected to benefit Railtown's AI Partner Marketplace, a commercial ecosystem designed to connect AI technology providers with prospective customers and support the commercialization of AI applications and services.

Through the Marketplace, participating technology partners will have the opportunity to incorporate Radium's models into AI solutions developed using Railtown's technology infrastructure.

This will provide partners with additional options when serving customers that prioritize Canadian data residency or require greater flexibility in selecting AI model providers.

Railtown believes that expanding the range of available AI technologies within its ecosystem will enhance the value of the Marketplace to participating companies and create additional opportunities for technology integration, customer acquisition and recurring platform revenue.

The partnership also supports Railtown's broader strategy of bringing together complementary AI technology providers through Conductr and its AI Partner Marketplace.

Radium Management Commentary

Adam Hendin, Cofounder / CEO of Radium, commented:

"Hal, Clarke and Tycho are built to stand alongside the frontier models, and Canadian companies should be able to run them at home. Railtown gives teams building agents on Conductr a direct way to do that."

About Radium

Radium is a frontier model alternative with drop-in LLM APIs to replace OpenAI and Anthropic. Its models, Hal, Clarke and Tycho, are served from Radium's own infrastructure, including in Canada. Radium is headquartered in San Francisco, with a second headquarters in Canada.

For more information, visit https://radium.cloud.

About Railtown AI Technologies Inc.

Railtown AI Technologies Inc. is an AI technology company developing tools and infrastructure that enable developers and organizations to build, deploy, manage and observe AI-powered applications and agents.

Its technology includes Conductr, an agentic AI orchestration, deployment and observability platform; Railengine, its knowledge and data infrastructure; and Railtracks, its open-source Agent Development Kit.

Railtown is focused on simplifying the development and operation of agentic applications while supporting organizations seeking flexible, secure and scalable AI solutions.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Talamore Mining Corp. (TSX: TALA) (OTCQX: TALMF) ("Talamore" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the successful completion of its previously announced warrant early exercise incentive program (the "Incentive Program"), resulting in significant strengthening of the Company's treasury and providing additional capital to advance development of its flagship Coffee Gold Project.

Under the Incentive Program, holders of eligible outstanding common share purchase warrants ("2025 Warrants") exercised a total of 31.3 million warrants at an exercise price of $2.50 per warrant, generating gross proceeds to the Company of approximately $78.3 million. Along with the equity financing completed in July 2026 and recently closed debt facility, the total financing package for the project is now $678 million.

Warrant holders were entitled to receive one half new common share purchase warrant ("Incentive Warrant") upon the exercise of each 2025 Warrant. The Incentive Warrants have an exercise price of $15.50 per share and will expire on October 15, 2033. The Company issued an aggregate of 15.6 million Incentive Warrants pursuant to the Incentive Program. Warrant holders that did not exercise will continue to hold their existing warrants.

"We are extremely pleased with the strong participation in the warrant incentive program," said Tim Warman, Chief Executive Officer of Talamore Mining. "The proceeds materially strengthen our balance sheet and provide additional financial flexibility as we continue to advance the Coffee Gold Project through development activities and key value-creation milestones. We appreciate the continued support and confidence shown by our shareholders."

About Talamore Mining

Talamore Mining Corp. is a Canadian exploration and development company advancing the Coffee Gold Project in Yukon, Canada. Coffee is a 100%-owned, open-pit heap leach gold project in the final stages of permitting and engineering, and the Company is working toward a construction decision. The project hosts 3.0 million ounces of Measured and Indicated resources and an additional 0.8 million ounces of Inferred resources. In addition to Coffee, Talamore holds a portfolio of copper and gold assets in Chile and Mexico, providing longer-term growth potential.

Talamore recognizes that protection of the land and water around the Coffee Gold Project is of central importance to the Trondëk Hwëch'in, White River First Nation, Selkirk First Nation, and the First Nation of Na-Cho Nyäk Dun. The Company is focused on building long-term relationships grounded in transparency, respect, and follow-through. MONTRÉAL, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- OR Royalties Inc. (“OR Royalties,” or the “Company”) (OR: TSX & NYSE) is pleased to provide select asset updates following Agnico Eagle Mines Limited’s (“Agnico Eagle”) Capital Markets Day held on November 18, 2026. Amounts presented are in United States dollars, except where otherwise noted.

For additional details on select royalties, please refer to OR Royalties’ 2026 Asset Handbook (link)

Summary Highlights

  • Canadian Malartic – pathway to ~1.0 Moz per year reaffirmed. Agnico Eagle outlined a pathway to approximately 1.0 million ounces (“Moz”) of annual gold (“Au”) production by 2033 at the Canadian Malartic Complex, comprising approximately 550 thousand ounces (“koz”) Au per year from Odyssey’s first shaft and ramp (2029), approximately 200-250koz Au from a potential second shaft, approximately 120-150koz Au from the Marban satellite open pit and approximately 80-100koz Au from the Wasamac satellite underground mine (each expected to start in 2033). The Canadian Malartic mill has a processing capacity of approximately 60,000 tonnes per day (“tpd”);
  • Odyssey Shaft #1 at 73% completion; first shaft production in June 2027. Agnico Eagle reports the project is on schedule to deliver the vision of its June 2023 updated preliminary economic assessment. Mining at the Barnat open pit safely restarted on schedule at the end of September 2026 following completion of remediation work;
  • Odyssey Shaft #2 defined. Conceptual design of 6.7 metres (“m”) in diameter and 1,740m in depth with potential ore capacity of 8,000-10,000tpd; technical studies to be completed in the second half of 2027; permit amendment expected in 2028; potential first production in 2033;
  • Upper Beaver; First production in the first half of 2030. Expected annual production of approximately 210koz Au and 3,600 tonnes of copper at 5,000tpd, scalable to 8,000tpd; updated technical evaluation expected in the second quarter of 2027; permits expected in early 2028;
  • Hammond Reef; Simple open-pit project with first production targeted for 2032. Preliminary parameters contemplate 250-300koz Au per year over a 13-year mine life from 3.3 Moz Au of Mineral Reserves (123.5 million tonnes (“Mt”) grading 0.84 grams per tonne (“g/t”) Au); updated technical evaluation in the second quarter of 2027; potential remaining permits and project approval in 2029; and,
  • A dense upcoming catalyst calendar. Updated technical evaluations for Upper Beaver and Hammond Reef in the second quarter of 2027, followed by completion of the Odyssey Shaft #2, Marban and Wasamac studies in the second half of 2027, are all expected to provide further definition on key assets within OR Royalties’ portfolio.

Jason Attew, President & CEO of OR Royalties, commented: “Agnico Eagle has done exactly what it said it would at Canadian Malartic: Shaft #1 is 73% complete, Barnat is back in production on schedule, and the path to roughly one million ounces a year by 2033 is now laid out shaft-by-shaft, and deposit-by-deposit. What matters most for our shareholders is the timing. Our existing portfolio already supports approximately 50% growth in attributable production to 2030. Odyssey’s second shaft, Marban in 2033, with Upper Beaver and Hammond Reef ramping through 2030 to 2032, extend our GEO1 growth well into the next decade, and the updated technical evaluations due in 2027 should also provide a crystal-clear roadmap of this expected growth for OR Royalties and its stakeholders.”

Canadian Malartic Complex: Pathway to ~1.0Moz of Annual Gold Production by 2033

OR Royalties’ interests. OR Royalties holds a 5.0% net smelter return (“NSR”) royalty on the Barnat pit and the low-grade stockpiles, a 5.0% NSR royalty on the East Gouldie and Odyssey South deposits and the western half of East Malartic, and a 3.0% NSR royalty on Odyssey North and the eastern half of East Malartic. Based on Agnico Eagle’s most recent published mine plan (2023), OR Royalties estimates a blended life-of-mine underground NSR royalty rate of approximately 4.61%.

At Marban, OR Royalties owns a 0.5% royalty over the Marban pit. OR Royalties also holds a C$0.40 per tonne royalty on any ore sourced from outside the royalty boundaries and processed through the Canadian Malartic mill, which would apply to any ore processed from Marban and Wasamac.

Canadian Malartic Complex; Barnat Pit and Shaft #1. The Canadian Malartic Complex (“Canadian Malartic”) is the second largest producing gold mine in Canada, with approximately 9.0Moz of gold in Proven and Probable Mineral Reserves as at December 31, 2025 (169.9Mt grading 1.66 g/t Au), and is soon transitioning to become the largest underground mine in Canada. Open pit mining at Barnat and processing of stockpiles are expected to continue until 2029, after which the complex transitions to underground production from Odyssey. Agnico Eagle reports that remediation work at the Barnat pit was completed and mining safely restarted at the end of September 2026, on schedule.

Underground production at Odyssey is currently via ramp, with the first four stopes at East Gouldie extracted year-to-date in 2026. Shaft #1 (1,586m deep) is 73% complete, with first production through the shaft expected in June 2027, the first loading station in H2 2027 and a second loading station in 2029. Agnico Eagle characterizes the project as on schedule to deliver the vision of its June 2023 updated preliminary economic assessment.

Figure 1. Canadian Malartic – Pathway to ~1 Moz of Annual Gold Production (Source: Agnico Eagle)

Odyssey Shaft #2. Agnico Eagle is advancing a potential second production shaft at Odyssey, with a conceptual design of 6.7m in diameter and 1,740m in depth and potential ore capacity of 8,000-10,000tpd. Technical studies are ongoing and expected to be completed in the second half of 2027 (“H2 2027”), with a permit amendment (decree modification and certificate of authorization) expected in 2028. This is all to be potentially followed by shaft sinking and underground development toward first targeted production in 2033. Technical studies on Shaft #2, along with a new Canadian Malartic life-of-mine plan, are ongoing and expected to be completed in H2 2027.

Figure 2. Shaft #2 Indicative Timeline; Potential First Production in 2033 (Source: Agnico Eagle)

Marban. Marban is a potential satellite open pit operation approximately 12 kilometres (“km”) from the Canadian Malartic mill, contemplated at 15,000-20,000tpd with anticipated annual gold production of approximately 120-150koz. Ore would be transported to the Canadian Malartic mill via a new production road, including the future construction of bridges above the highway and railroad. Marban hosts 1.6 Moz Au of Probable Mineral Reserves (51.6Mt grading 0.95 g/t Au) as at December 31, 2025. Technical studies are expected to be completed in H2 2027, receipt of federal and provincial permits is expected in 2031 and first production could occur as early as 2033.

Figure 3. Marban Indicative Timeline; Potential First Production in 2033 (Source: Agnico Eagle)

Upper Beaver: Production Ramp-Up in H1 2030 & Potential Mill Expansion to 8,000tpd

OR Royalties’ interests. OR Royalties owns a 2.0% NSR royalty on Upper Beaver. OR Royalties owns a 2.0% NSR royalty that covers most of Agnico’s Kirkland Lake regional properties, including AK, Upper Canada and Anoki-McBean.

Upper Beaver. Upper Beaver is an underground gold-copper project in Agnico Eagle’s Kirkland Lake camp with expected annual production of approximately 210koz Au, along with approximately 3,600 tonnes of copper (“Cu”), beginning in 2030. The planned processing rate is 5,000tpd, and Agnico Eagle is now evaluating a scale-up of the mill to 8,000tpd. Agnico Eagle is advancing an exploration ramp and an exploration shaft, with the shaft to reach 760m and a potential extension to 1,220m. Milestones include access to the 160 level for a bulk sample in the first half of 2027, an updated technical evaluation in the second quarter of 2027 (“Q2 2027”), receipt of permits in early 2028 and underground production ramp-up in the first half of 2030, subject to receipt of all key permits.

Anoki McBean & Upper Canada. Agnico Eagle is developing a full-potential model focused on the Upper Canada and Anoki-McBean satellite deposits, which it envisions as potential satellite mines leveraging expanded mill capacity at Upper Beaver. As at December 31, 2025, Anoki-McBean hosts 0.3Moz Au of Indicated Mineral Resources (3.9Mt grading 2.77 g/t Au) and 0.1Moz Au of Inferred Mineral Resources (0.9Mt grading 3.84 g/t Au), and Upper Canada hosts 0.8Moz Au of Indicated Mineral Resources (11.0Mt grading 2.3 g/t Au) and 2.2Moz Au of Inferred Mineral Resources (24.1Mt grading 2.85 g/t Au). Technical and economic evaluations of both deposits are ongoing, and Agnico Eagle is also currently developing a first-pass “full-potential” model of these satellite operations.

Figure 4. Upper Beaver Indicative Timeline; Potential First Production in H1 2030 (Source: Agnico Eagle)

Hammond Reef: Open-Pit Project in Ontario with Potential First Production in 2032

OR Royalties’ interest. OR Royalties owns a 2.0% NSR royalty on Hammond Reef.

Hammond Reef. Hammond Reef is located in northwestern Ontario near Atikokan and is a high-tonnage, low-grade gold deposit with potential for development as a two-pit operation with conventional milling and a low strip ratio of approximately 1.3:1. Preliminary project parameters contemplate a mining rate of approximately 100,000tpd, a processing rate of 33,500tpd, annual gold production of 250-300koz and a 13-year mine life. The project hosts 3.3Moz Au of Probable Mineral Reserves (123.5Mt grading 0.84 g/t Au) and 2.3Moz Au of Measured and Indicated Mineral Resources (133.4Mt grading 0.54 g/t Au). A 19km, 230 kilovolt transmission line and a 38km all-weather access road upgrade are required for project development.

Agnico Eagle is advancing optimization studies and final permits required for construction and operation. An updated technical evaluation is expected in Q2 2027, with potential receipt of permits and project approval in 2029 and potential production ramp-up in 2032.

Figure 5. Hammond Reef Indicative Timeline; Potential First Production in 2032 (Source: Agnico Eagle)

Autozi formally enters the execution phase of its systematic acquisition program, seeking to build a larger, technology-driven supply-chain services platform and enter a new stage of development

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Autozi Internet Technology (Global) Ltd. (Nasdaq: AZI) (the “Company” or “Autozi”), a technology-driven provider of lifecycle automotive services, today announced the formal launch of its continuous business acquisition strategy following more than a year of work on establishing its red-chip structure, optimizing corporate governance and conducting business due diligence.

The Company’s first acquisition target is Zhiyun Zhongka Group Global Limited, which operates under the market brand “Zhongka” (“Zhongka”). Autozi currently expects the first transaction to close on or before November 30, 2026, subject to the completion of definitive transaction documents, the satisfaction or waiver of closing conditions, required corporate and regulatory approvals, and other customary requirements.

Autozi believes the expected closing of its first transaction will mark an important transition from strategic preparation to active execution. The Company intends to continue pursuing acquisitions and strategic integration opportunities to add operating scale, fulfillment infrastructure, customer resources, technology capabilities and complementary product categories to its existing platform.

Complementary Business Advantages

Business Synergies Expanding Revenue and Market Coverage

The acquisition of Zhongka’s supply-chain business is expected to create a dual-market structure covering both the automotive aftermarket and the broader consumer sector, including vehicles, automotive parts and consumer products. The Company believes this expanded business portfolio can significantly enhance its market presence and industry position.

Complementary Fulfillment Networks Connecting an Asset-Light Platform with Warehousing and Distribution Infrastructure

Autozi operates an asset-light digital platform model, while Zhongka operates more than 150,000 square meters of multi-temperature warehousing facilities across seven major regions in China. Zhongka’s network covers more than 200 cities and has a peak daily order-processing capacity exceeding one million orders.

Zhongka’s nationwide integrated warehousing and distribution capabilities are expected to provide a strong physical fulfillment foundation for Autozi’s supply-chain business, creating a more complete combination of digital platform capabilities and physical infrastructure.

Digital Integration Building a Unified Transaction and Fulfillment Platform

Autozi plans to integrate its industrial internet platform with Zhongka’s end-to-end e-commerce systems, including order management, warehousing, financial management and application programming interface connections with major e-commerce platforms.

The planned integration is expected to create a unified digital platform covering both transaction management and fulfillment, providing customers across both business sectors with more efficient end-to-end services.

Management Commentary

Mr. Houqi Zhang, Chief Executive Officer of Autozi, commented:

“Zhongka Supply Chain has established a strong warehousing and distribution network and valuable brand-customer resources. This acquisition represents an important step in Autozi’s development of a multi-industry supply-chain services platform. We intend to fully leverage the complementary capabilities of both companies and create long-term value for our shareholders.”

About Autozi

Autozi Internet Technology (Global) Ltd. (Nasdaq: AZI) is a leading digital supply-chain services platform serving China’s automotive industry. The Company provides integrated transaction, fulfillment and supply-chain finance services to vehicle manufacturers, insurance companies, automotive parts manufacturers and automotive repair and maintenance service providers.

About Zhongka Supply Chain

Zhongka Supply Chain was established in 2019 and operates a service platform centered on social commerce and origin-based end-to-end logistics and supply-chain services.

Zhongka provides nationwide integrated warehousing and distribution services covering temperature ranges from ambient storage to deep-frozen storage. It operates more than 150,000 square meters of warehousing facilities, serves more than 3,000 brands and has a peak daily order volume exceeding one million orders.

Zhongka’s investors include Xingtuo Capital, Yaowang Technology Co., Ltd. (002291.SZ) and Better Life Group.

The Company believes that, in addition to financial measures and ratios prepared in accordance with IFRS, certain investors use these non-IFRS financial measures and ratios to evaluate the Company's performance. However, the measures do not have a standardized meaning under IFRS and may not be comparable to similar financial measures disclosed by other companies. Accordingly, non-IFRS financial measures and non-IFRS ratios should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures and ratios of the Company's performance prepared in accordance with IFRS.

Non-IFRS financial measures are defined in National Instrument 52-112 - Non-GAAP and Other Financial Measures Disclosure ("NI 52-112") as a financial measure disclosed that (a) depicts the historical or expected future financial performance, financial position or cash flow of an entity, (b) with respect to its composition, excludes an amount that is included in, or includes an amount that is excluded from, the composition of the most directly comparable financial measure disclosed in the primary financial statements of the entity, (c) is not disclosed in the financial statements of the entity, and (d) is not a ratio, fraction, percentage or similar representation.

A non-IFRS ratio is defined by NI 52-112 as a financial measure disclosed that (a) is in the form of a ratio, fraction, percentage, or similar representation, (b) has a non-IFRS financial measure as one or more of its components, and (c) is not disclosed in the financial statements.

WORKING CAPITAL

Working capital is a non-IFRS measure that is a common measure of liquidity but does not have any standardized meaning. The most directly comparable measure prepared in accordance with IFRS is current assets net of current liabilities. Working capital is calculated by deducting current liabilities from current assets. Working capital should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures prepared in accordance with IFRS. The measure is intended to assist readers in evaluating the Company's liquidity.

MINE OPERATING CASH FLOW BEFORE TAXES

Mine operating cash flow before taxes is a non-IFRS measure that does not have a standardized meaning prescribed by IFRS and therefore may not be comparable to similar measures presented by other issuers. Mine operating cash flow is calculated as revenue minus production costs, transportation and selling costs and inventory changes. Mine operating cash flow is used by management to assess the performance of the mine operations, excluding corporate and exploration activities, and is provided to investors as a measure of the Company's operating performance.

EBITDA

EBITDA is a non-IFRS financial measure, which excludes the following from net earnings:

  • Income tax expense;
  • Finance costs;
  • Amortization and depletion.

Adjusted EBITDA excludes the following additional items from EBITDA:

  • Share based compensation;
  • Impairments (reversals);
  • Loss (gain) on derivative;
  • Unrealized foreign exchange (gain) loss relating to ARO
  • Significant other finance items.

Adjusted EBITDA per share is calculated by dividing Adjusted EBITDA by the basic weighted average number of shares outstanding for the period.

Management believes EBITDA is a valuable indicator of the Company's ability to generate liquidity by producing operating cash flow to fund working capital needs, service debt obligations, and fund capital expenditures. Management uses EBITDA for this purpose. EBITDA is also frequently used by investors and analysts for valuation purposes whereby EBITDA is multiplied by a factor or "EBITDA multiple" based on an observed or inferred relationship between EBITDA and market values to determine the approximate total enterprise value of a Company. Management believes that Adjusted EBITDA provides useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results because it is consistent with the indicators management uses internally to measure the Company's performance and is an indicator of the performance of the Company's mining operations.

EBITDA is intended to provide additional information to investors and analysts. It does not have any standardized definition under IFRS and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures of operating performance prepared in accordance with IFRS. EBITDA excludes the impact of cash costs of financing activities and taxes, and the effects of changes in operating working capital balances and therefore is not necessarily indicative of operating profit or cash flow from operations as determined by IFRS. Other companies may calculate EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA differently.

Cash Cost per AgEq Ounce, All-In Sustaining Cost per AgEq Ounce and Production Cost per Tonne

Cash costs per silver equivalent ounce and production costs per tonne are measures developed by precious metals companies in an effort to provide a comparable standard; however, there can be no assurance that the Company's reporting of these non-IFRS measures and ratios are similar to those reported by other mining companies. Cash costs per silver equivalent ounce and total production cost per tonne are non-IFRS performance measures used by the Company to manage and evaluate operating performance at its operating mining unit, in conjunction with the related IFRS amounts. They are widely reported in the silver mining industry as a benchmark for performance, but do not have a standardized meaning and are disclosed in addition to IFRS measures. Production costs include mining, milling, and direct overhead at the operation sites. Cash costs include all direct costs plus royalties. Total production costs include all cash costs plus amortization and depletion, changes in amortization and depletion in finished goods inventory and site share-based compensation. Cash costs per silver equivalent ounce is calculated by dividing cash costs and total production costs by the payable silver ounces produced. Production costs per tonne are calculated by dividing production costs by the number of processed tonnes. The following tables provide a detailed reconciliation of these measures to the Company's direct production costs, as reported in its consolidated financial statements.

AISC is a non-IFRS performance measure and was calculated based on guidance provided by the World Gold Council ("WGC"). WGC is not a regulatory industry organization and does not have the authority to develop accounting standards for disclosure requirements. Other mining companies may calculate AISC differently as a result of differences in underlying accounting principles and policies applied, as well as differences in definitions of sustaining capital expenditures. AISC is a more comprehensive measure than cash cost per ounce and is useful for investors and management to assess the Company's operating performance by providing greater visibility, comparability and representation of the total costs associated with producing silver from its current operations, in conjunction with related IFRS amounts. AISC helps investors to assess costs against peers in the industry and help management assess the performance of its mine.

AISC includes total production costs (IFRS measure) incurred at the Company's mining operation, which forms the basis of the Company's total cash costs. Additionally, the Company includes sustaining capital expenditures, corporate general and administrative expense, operating lease payments and reclamation cost accretion. The Company believes this measure represents the total sustainable costs of producing silver and gold concentrate from current operations and provides additional information of the Company's operational performance and ability to generate cash flows. As the measure seeks to reflect the full cost of silver and gold concentrate production from current operations, new project capital is not included. Certain other cash and non-cash expenditures, including share-based payments, tax payments, dividends and financing costs are also not included.

Company gains access to more than 53 million U.S. buyers on a platform where beauty is the top category and products listing peptides as an ingredient command the highest average price of any top 10 beauty ingredient

Highlights

  • Approved TikTok Shop storefront: The Company has been approved to operate its own TikTok Shop in the United States, giving it a direct sales channel to more than 53 million U.S. buyers.
  • Approved under tighter rules: The approval follows TikTok's October 2026 move to restrict searches for several peptide names and its stated prohibition on marketing high-risk products.
  • Rollout underway: The first product is live, with further products from the Company's U.S.-made range being brought to the shop, each through TikTok Shop's product review.
  • Peptide products sell at a premium: Beauty products listing peptides as an ingredient generated USD 73.2 million in TikTok Shop sales at a USD 50 average price, the highest of any top 10 beauty ingredient.
  • Verified quality: Every product is made in an approved U.S. facility and backed by a third-party Certificate of Analysis.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - The Precision Peptide Company (CSE: BPC) (OTCQB: PNGAF) (the "Company"), a publicly traded wellness company focused on advanced peptide formulations and delivery systems, today announced that it has been approved to operate a TikTok Shop storefront in the United States. The first product is now live, with further products from its U.S.-made range to be added as each completes the platform's product review.

The approval comes as TikTok tightens its standards on peptide content, and gives the Company a direct channel to TikTok Shop's 53 million U.S. buyers at a moment when beauty is the platform's largest category, haircare sales have more than doubled, and beauty products listing peptides as an ingredient sell at the highest average price of any leading ingredient.

Approved as TikTok Raises the Bar

In October 2026, TikTok began restricting searches for several peptide names. The platform has said that peptide discussion remains permitted, but that it prohibits the marketing of high-risk products and may restrict searches for unapproved or potentially unsafe products.[10]

The Company's shop was reviewed and approved under those standards. Every product it brings to the platform is manufactured in an approved U.S. facility and supported by a third-party Certificate of Analysis, and as a publicly traded company it reports to shareholders under Canadian securities regulation.

Ingredient-First Products, Rolling Out

With its storefront approved, the Company is bringing its range to the shop product by product, each through TikTok Shop's product review. Every listing names the peptides inside, so shoppers can see exactly what they are buying.

HAIR, the Company's scalp and hair serum, shows the approach. Designed for women who want thicker-looking, fuller-looking hair, it is a simple daily scalp step built around GHK-Cu (Copper Tripeptide-1), the copper peptide that gives the serum its natural blue color. That color is a visible signature of the ingredient, and it comes through on camera, where TikTok Shop products are discovered and sold. HAIR opens the shop in haircare, a category where TikTok Shop sales more than doubled year over year.[7]

Why TikTok Shop

TikTok Shop's U.S. gross merchandise value (GMV) reached USD 15.1 billion in 2025, up 68% from 2024.[1] It then reached USD 11.8 billion in the first half of 2026 alone, up 103% year over year, making the U.S. the platform's largest market.[2] eMarketer forecasts U.S. TikTok Shop sales of USD 23.41 billion for full-year 2026.[3]

The platform had 53.2 million U.S. buyers in 2025,[4] and more of them now arrive with intent: in the first half of 2026, the Shop tab drove 51.4% of U.S. GMV, ahead of video and LIVE.[2] Shoppers who search by ingredient reward brands that can name exactly what is in the bottle, which is how the Company formulates and labels its range.

Beauty & Personal Care is TikTok Shop's largest U.S. category, with an estimated USD 413.1 million in GMV in September 2026, or 17.1% of all U.S. GMV,[5] and USD 1.21 billion across Q3 2026.[6] Haircare alone generated USD 401.1 million in Q2 2026, up 118% year over year.[7] Within beauty, products listing peptides as an ingredient generated USD 73.2 million in sales at a USD 50 average price, the highest of any top 10 ingredient,[9] and four of the top five beauty products in Q2 2026 featured longevity ingredients,[8] a core focus of the Company's peptide formulations.

TikTok Shop extends the Company's direct-to-consumer e-commerce store, its telehealth platform serving all 50 U.S. states, and the nationwide retail sale of its U.S.-made over-the-counter range, which began on July 30, 2026. The launch delivers on distribution expansion, one of the 2027 growth priorities the Company set out in its November 11, 2026 year-end update.

"Winning approval for a TikTok Shop at the same time the platform is tightening its rules on peptides is a real milestone for us," said Pratap Sandhu, CEO of The Precision Peptide Company. "TikTok holds anyone in the peptide space to a high bar, and we built our range to meet it. Every product we bring to the platform is U.S.-made and backed by third-party testing. Our first product is live, and we will keep adding to the shop as each one clears review. This is a bigger step into social commerce for the Company, and we intend to build on it."

Montréal, Québec--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Amex Gold Mining Inc. (TSXV: AMX) (FSE: MX00) (OTCQX: AMXEF) ("Amex" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the achievement of several important underground development and infrastructure milestones at its 100%-owned Perron Gold Project, located near Normétal, Québec, including:

  • 200 metres of underground ramp development completed, marking continued progress toward the fully funded 40,000-tonne bulk sample program.

  • Construction of the 25-kV power line is underway. This power line is designed with capacity to support both the bulk sample program and the future Phase 1 mining operation.

  • Mechanical garage structure has been installed. Majority of the bulk sample site facilities have now been erected and are nearing completion.

Together, these infrastructure improvements contribute to establishing the operational foundation required for the bulk sample and the next stages of underground development and future Phase 1 mining operation at Perron.

Underground Ramp Development Reaches 200 Metres

Underground development at Perron continues to progress, with the main access ramp reaching 200 metres of completed development. To date progress has been steady and on time per construction plans.

Construction of the Power Line Underway

Construction of the approximately 6.5-kilometre, 25-kV power line connecting the Perron Gold Project to the existing electrical grid in Normétal is underway.

The power line is designed to provide approximately 3 MW of electrical capacity, sufficient to support both the ongoing 40,000-tonne bulk sample program and the planned Phase 1 mining operation, as outlined in the Company's Feasibility Study released in April 2026.

This investment represents a step forward in establishing the long-term infrastructure required for Perron. By developing an electrical connection capable of serving both the current bulk sample program and future Phase 1 operations, Amex is strategically positioning the project for its next stage of development while minimizing the need for additional major electrical infrastructure investments.

Once operational, the power line is expected to provide reliable clean hydroelectricity to underground and surface facilities while reducing reliance on diesel-powered generation.
