Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - NexMetals Mining Corp. (TSXV: NEXM) (NASDAQ: NEXM) ("NexMetals" or the "Company") is pleased to report assay results from drill holes SMD-26-217 and SMD-26-216-W1, part of its ongoing surface drilling program at the Selebi Main deposit in Botswana (see Figure 1). The results indicate a newly encountered third mineralized zone below the Lower Zone (the "Third Zone") and extension of the interpreted high-grade trend by approximately 100 metres toward Selebi North, bringing its interpreted length to approximately 1.5 kilometres (the "High-Grade Trend").

SMD-26-217 intersected three distinct mineralized zones. The Main Zone returned 3.15 metres grading 3.14% Cu and 0.86% Ni. The Lower Zone returned 6.60 metres grading 1.35% Cu and 1.95% Ni including 4.25 metres grading 1.33% Cu and 2.37% Ni. The newly encountered Third Zone returned 6.30 metres grading 2.67% Cu and 1.85% Ni, including 4.30 metres grading 2.98% Cu and 2.38% Ni, with higher copper grades than those of the Lower Zone potentially indicating greater remobilization.

SMD-26-216-W1 was an in-fill hole testing a sparsely drilled area approximately 165 metres north of the High-Grade Trend. The hole intersected 1.00 metre grading 2.98% Cu and 1.07% Ni corresponding to the Main Zone and a Lower Zone interval of 3.45 metres grading 2.86% Cu and 1.52% Ni, including 1.45 metres grading 3.61% Cu and 1.94% Ni. SMD-26-216-W1 infills a gap within the resource model on the northern side of the mineralized trend and supports the interpreted consistency of the High-Grade Trend and lateral continuity of the mineralized zones.

Why This Matters

  • New Third Zone expands the exploration opportunity at Selebi Main. NexMetals' first significant intersection below the Lower Zone returned higher copper grades than the Lower Zone in the same hole, alongside strong nickel grades, and indicates increased structural complexity as drilling advances toward Selebi North.

  • The High-Grade Trend has been extended toward Selebi North. SMD-26-217 extendsthe High-Grade Trend to 1.5 kilometres and extended it by approximately 100 metres toward Selebi North while SMD-26-216-W1 supports lateral continuity in the up-dip direction.

  • Lower Zone is demonstrating increasing continuity at depth. Results from SMD-26-213 (7.45 metres grading 2.52% Cu, 1.54% Ni, see news release dated July 22, 2026), SMD-26-219 (7.55 metres grading 2.70% Cu and 1.83% Ni, see news release dated September 23, 2026, together with SMD-26-217 (6.60 metres grading 1.35% Cu and 1.95% Ni, current release) support the interpretation of a laterally and vertically extensive Lower Zone.

  • The system remains open, with further targets to test. Borehole electromagnetic surveying ("BHEM") indicates additional potential mineralization laterally and down plunge. Ongoing drilling and geological modelling are intended to test the extent of all three mineralized zones and target additional areas of thick massive sulphide mineralization.

Sean Whiteford, CEO and Director of the Company, commented: "Our first intersection of the Third Zone returned strong copper and nickel grades below the Lower Zone, providing an additional target for follow-up drilling. Building on the recent 72% increase in Selebi Main's Inferred Mineral Resource to 32.47 million tonnes grading 1.53% copper and 0.97% nickel, these results point to further growth potential as we continue to test the limits of the deposit. SMD-26-217 extends the interpreted High-Grade Trend toward Selebi North, while SMD-26-216-W1 supports potential lateral continuity. We are advancing technical and trade-off studies to support the preliminary economic assessment, while continuing exploration drilling to test the open system."

Qualified Person

All scientific and technical information in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Sharon Taylor, V.P. Geophysics of the Company, MSc, P.Geo, and a "qualified person" for the purposes of National Instrument 43-101 and Subpart 1300 of Regulation S-K.

Quality Control and Data Verification

The program is being executed using three Company-owned underground Zinex U5 drills which were converted into surface A5 drills, and two Marcotte HTM2500 drills purchased by the Company capable of drilling to depths of 2,550 metres (NQ core).

Drill core samples are either NQ (47.75 mm diameter) or BQ (36.40 mm diameter). All samples are ½ core samples cut by a diamond saw on site and the remaining half of the core is retained for reference purposes. Samples are generally 1.0 to 1.5 metre intervals or less at the discretion of the site geologists. Sample preparation and lab analysis were completed at ALS Geochemistry in Johannesburg, South Africa. Commercially prepared blank samples and certified Cu/Ni sulphide analytical control standards with a range of grades are inserted in every batch of 20 samples or a minimum of one set per sample batch. Analyses for Ni, Cu and Co are completed using a peroxide fusion preparation and ICP-AES finish (ME-ICP81). Analyses for Pt, Pd, and Au are by fire assay (30 grams nominal sample weight) with an ICP-AES finish (PGM-ICP23).

Holes are numbered as follows: SMD (Selebi Main Deposit) + year + hole number starting at 201.

The Qualified Person has verified the data disclosed in this news release, including the sampling, analytical and test data underlying the information, through contribution to the core handling and sampling procedures, visits to the drill and core processing facilities, monitoring of core logging results and sample selection, review of core assay and QA/QC results.

BHEM Surveys

The BHEM surveys at Selebi utilize the Crone PEM system operated by local Botswana staff. Survey data is collected using a 3-component fluxgate probe collecting full waveform data. Surveys have been collected using timebases between 50 and 1000ms (0.25 Hz to 5 Hz). The data has been processed to a calculated residual step response to better quantify the conductive sources. This added processing has proven to be highly valuable because of the size of the highly conductive mineralized system.

Cape Town, South Africa--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Lithium Africa Corp. (TSXV: LAF) (FSE: 6MQ) (OTCQB: LTAFF) ("Lithium Africa" or the "Company"), the hard-rock lithium explorer and developer targeting district-scale opportunities across Africa, is pleased to report the discovery of a new lithium-bearing pegmatite system at Jackal Water, 11 km southwest of the Norrabees cluster at its Springbok Project in the Northern Cape of South Africa (the "Springbok Project" or "Springbok"). The first holes intersected stacked pegmatites with up to 56 meters ("m") of logged pegmatite downhole and returned lithium grades of up to 2.21% lithium oxide ("Li2O") over 1.0 m. Together with the Norrabees cluster results reported on November 17, 2026, the Company believes the discovery shows that lithium-bearing pegmatites at Springbok extend well beyond Norrabees, across a district similar in geological style to Brazil's Lithium Valley.

Highlights

  • A new discovery by Lithium Africa's team: Jackal Water was identified using the Company's proprietary, machine-learning-assisted targeting method, developed in-house. The pegmatites are 11 km southwest of the Norrabees cluster and have no known record of previous exploration or drilling (Figure 1).

  • Thick, stacked pegmatites with lithium: all eight reverse circulation ("RC") holes intersected pegmatite, with 11 m to 56 m of logged pegmatite downhole. First assays, received from three of the eight holes, returned 1.0 m intervals of 2.21%, 1.35%, and 0.89% Li2O (Table 1, Appendix). The remaining pegmatite assayed to date returned no significant intercepts, assays are pending from five of the eight holes, and true widths are not yet known.

  • Wide pegmatites along a 50 km trend: spodumene-bearing pegmatites at Springbok are 9 m to 30 m wide in outcrop (not true thickness), along a trend of approximately 50 km on a single 1,675 km² license, and drilling at Jackal Water intersected up to 56 m of logged pegmatite downhole (true width not yet known). For context, Sigma Lithium reports that its Xuxa pegmatite in Brazil's Lithium Valley averages 12 m to 13 m thick; this is not necessarily indicative of mineralization at Springbok.

  • Additional near-surface lithium at Norrabees I: diamond hole NB1DD26-006 returned 9.05 m at 1.19% Li2O from 1.95 m downhole, including 6.0 m at 1.44% Li2O, inside the Company's five-hectare mining permit (Table 1, Appendix).

"Our discovery at Jackal Water takes Springbok from a cluster to a district," said Thomas R. Benson, Ph.D., CEO of Lithium Africa. "Eleven kilometers from Norrabees, our first holes intersected up to 56 m of logged pegmatite downhole and returned up to 2.21% Li2O over 1.0 m. Our project hosts an approximately 50 km trend of lithium-bearing pegmatites similar in thickness to those of Brazil's Lithium Valley, including Sigma Lithium's Xuxa mine (~12-13 m on average), and the results are just starting to come in."

Jackal Water Discovery

The Jackal Water pegmatites (Figure 1) were identified through the Company's in-house targeting method, which combines satellite imagery with machine-learning-assisted analysis of handheld pXRF data, and were confirmed by field mapping. They have no known record of previous exploration or drilling. Eight RC holes (308 m) tested the Jackal Water I and Jackal Water II pegmatites, and all eight intersected pegmatite: 11 m to 24 m downhole at Jackal Water I and 12 m to 56 m downhole at Jackal Water II.

At Jackal Water I, JW1RC26-002 returned 1.0 m at 2.21% Li2O from 10 m and 1.0 m at 0.89% Li2O from 15 m, with elevated cesium ("Cs") and rubidium ("Rb"). At Jackal Water II, JW2RC26-003 intersected 56 m of pegmatite to 57 m downhole and returned 1.0 m at 1.35% Li2O from 45 m, within a 42 m to 47 m zone with elevated Cs and tantalum ("Ta"); the remaining assayed pegmatite returned less than 0.25% Li2O. JW1RC26-003 returned no significant intercept, and assays are pending for the other five holes and for parts of JW1RC26-002 and JW2RC26-003 (Table 1, Appendix).

The Company interprets the enrichment in cesium, tantalum, and rubidium as an indication that highly fractionated pegmatites with the potential to host lithium mineralization occur at both the Norrabees cluster and Jackal Water. This interpretation is preliminary and remains to be tested by further drilling and assays. Intervals and logged pegmatite thicknesses are downhole lengths; true widths are not yet known, and logged pegmatite thickness is not a measure of lithium grade. Collar details are in Table 2 (Appendix).

Three follow-up RC holes (189 m) have since been drilled at Jackal Water, with assays pending, and the Company plans further drilling to test the extent of the pegmatites.



Figure 1: The Springbok Project Prospecting Right (1,675 km²), Northern Cape, South Africa, showing the Jackal Water I and II discovery, the Norrabees cluster and five-hectare mining permit, mapped spodumene occurrences, and key infrastructure. Callouts show selected results from this release and a previously reported result from Norrabees I (see news release dated September 30, 2026). Intervals are downhole lengths, and true widths are not yet known (Table 1, Appendix). Inset shows the Springbok Project location.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/11554/324825_d935e21414d28b19_001full.jpg

District-Scale Exploration Potential and Comparison to Brazil's Lithium Valley

Spodumene-bearing pegmatites at Springbok are 9 m to 30 m wide in outcrop, as described in the Company's technical report dated July 21, 2026, along a trend of approximately 50 km on a single 1,675 km² license (Figure 2). Drilling at Jackal Water intersected up to 56 m of logged pegmatite downhole (true widths are not yet known), which the Company believes further supports the potential for thick lithium-bearing pegmatites across the district. For context, Sigma Lithium Corporation's technical report dated March 31, 2025 on its Grota do Cirilo project in Brazil's Lithium Valley describes pegmatites that average 12 m to 13 m thick at Xuxa and are 30 m to 35 m thick at Barreiro, and Pedrosa-Soares et al. (2025, Economic Geology, v. 120, no. 5) describe the pegmatites mined at Cachoeira since 1992 as decimeters to 30 m thick. This information is from the public sources cited and has not been verified by the Company or its Qualified Person. Outcrop widths and downhole intervals are not true thicknesses and are not on the same basis as the thicknesses reported in Brazil, and the comparison is of pegmatite thickness only, not of strike length, grade, tonnage, or mineralogy. The Springbok Project has no mineral resource estimate, and mineralization in Brazil is not necessarily indicative of mineralization at Springbok.



Figure 2: Brazil's Lithium Valley (Minas Gerais) and South Africa's Springbok District (Northern Cape) at the same map scale, showing license areas, mapped spodumene occurrences, and selected pegmatites. Thicknesses shown for Brazil are from Sigma Lithium Corporation's technical report dated March 31, 2025, and Pedrosa-Soares et al. (2025); Springbok outcrop widths are from the Company's technical report dated July 21, 2026, and are not true thicknesses. Information on Brazil is from public sources, has not been verified by the Company or its Qualified Person, and is not necessarily indicative of mineralization at Springbok, which has no mineral resource estimate.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/11554/324825_d935e21414d28b19_002full.jpg

Drilling Continues Across the Springbok District

Drilling is continuing across the Springbok District to further define the potential of the Springbok Project. In 2026 the Company has drilled 138 holes across 14 pegmatite targets for approximately 4,330 m, including three follow-up holes (189 m) at Jackal Water and holes at Blesberg I (five holes, 105 m), Uranoop (seven holes, 182 m), Frankie (seven holes, 161 m), Kokerboomrand (eight holes, 280 m), and Spodumene Kop (16 holes, approximately 520 m) (Figure 2). Assays are pending, and results will be reported as they are received and validated.

At Norrabees I, diamond hole NB1DD26-006, collared inside the Company's five-hectare mining permit, returned 9.05 m at 1.19% Li2O from 1.95 m downhole, including 6.0 m at 1.44% Li2O from 4.0 m. Results from all 10 holes received from Norrabees I, V, and VIII, including holes with no significant intercepts, are in Table 1 (Appendix). Intervals are downhole lengths, and true widths are not yet known.

Sampling, Analysis, QA/QC and Data Verification

RC drilling was completed by Van Zyl Drilling using a face-sampling hammer. RC samples were collected over 1 m intervals through a riffle splitter, and a representative chip sample from each interval was retained in chip trays for logging. Diamond core from NB1DD26-005 and NB1DD26-006 was logged and sampled at nominal 1 m intervals adjusted to lithological contacts, and half-core was submitted for analysis. Sampling covered the logged pegmatite and 1 m to 2 m of adjacent host rock on either side of each pegmatite interval. Samples of approximately 2 kg were bagged, ticketed and sent to SGS South Africa (Randfontein) ("SGS"), an independent commercial laboratory accredited by SANAS to ISO/IEC 17025. Lithium was analyzed by sodium peroxide fusion with an ICP-AES finish (GE_ICP90A50) and a multi-element suite including cesium, rubidium and tantalum by sodium peroxide fusion with an ICP-MS finish (GE_IMS90A50).

The Company inserted a certified reference material every 20 samples, a blank every 50 samples, and a field duplicate every 10 samples. All certified reference material lithium results were within three standard deviations of the certified values, and all blanks returned lithium below or at the 10 ppm detection limit. Field duplicates showed acceptable repeatability, other than two core duplicate pairs from the spodumene-bearing interval in NB1DD26-006 and pairs below 200 ppm Li, where relative differences are large close to the detection limit. SGS's internal standards, blanks and repeats were also reviewed. Collar locations were recorded by handheld GPS.

The Qualified Person, Benjamin Gelber, P.Geo., has verified the assay database against the original laboratory certificates and considers the QA/QC results acceptable for the purpose of this release.

Qualified Person

The technical and scientific information in this news release was reviewed, verified and approved by Benjamin Gelber, P.Geo., a consultant of the Company and a practicing Professional Geologist registered with Engineers & Geoscientists British Columbia (EGBC, Licence No. 33258), who is a non-independent "Qualified Person" as defined by National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects. The information on Brazil in this news release is taken from the public sources cited and has not been verified by the Qualified Person, and drill collar locations were recorded by handheld GPS. No other limitations on, or failures of, verification were identified.

Lithium Africa Corp. is a lithium exploration and development company building a portfolio of hard-rock lithium assets across Africa. The Company holds the Springbok Project in South Africa directly and its exploration interests in West and Southern Africa, including the Adzopé District in Côte d'Ivoire, through a 50/50 joint venture with GFL International Co., Ltd., an affiliate of Ganfeng Lithium.   • The Gleeson Project is Located on Private Land 28 Miles North of the Famous and Historic Bisbee Mining District
  • Intercepts Include 123.6 Meters Grading 0.91% Copper, 0.44 g/t Gold, and 5.27 g/t Silver from 601.70 Meters
  • Drilling Occurring on a Small Portion of Ivanhoe Electric's Land Package Consisting of Approximately 20,000 Acres of Mineral Rights and over 2,000 Acres of Private Surface Rights
  • Two Drill Rigs are Active with Further Assays to be Received in Coming Weeks

Phoenix, Arizona--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Ivanhoe Electric Inc. (NYSE American: IE) (TSX: IE) ("Ivanhoe Electric") Executive Chairman Robert Friedland and President and Chief Executive Officer Taylor Melvin are pleased to report the discovery of copper-gold-silver mineralization in the first drill holes on private land at the Company's Gleeson Copper-Gold Project ("Gleeson"). Gleeson is located in the historical Courtland-Gleeson Mining District in southeastern Arizona, 28 miles north of the world-famous historical Bisbee Mining District.

Mines in the Bisbee Mining District produced from 1880 to 2013 exploiting breccia, carbonate and intrusive-hosted deposits similar to mineralization styles at Gleeson.

Results from the first eleven completed drill holes have discovered two separate, significant mineralized domains at Gleeson below low angle faulting. Copper-gold-silver breccia has been logged in drill holes spanning an area of approximately 500 by 500 meters, from 600 meters depth, pinching out in the east to over 380 meters downhole thickness in the south-west. The breccia remains open in multiple directions. Below 1,000 meters depth, intrusive and carbonate replacement hosted copper-gold-silver-zinc mineralization has been discovered with mineralization logged in drillholes over 800 meters of north to south extent, 600 meters east to west and a strong vector to the west.

Ivanhoe Electric's Senior Vice President of Exploration, Alex Neufeld, commented: "The initial drill holes at Gleeson are the most impressive I have seen in my 20-year career at an early-stage exploration project. We are excited to announce that we have discovered two significant mineralized domains, with high-grade breccias and carbonate replacement mineralization. This is just the start of our search in this underappreciated, historic mining district which at this early stage is showing evidence that it may be analogous to the mineralization that underpinned the more than century of historic mining at Bisbee."

Highlights from the first holes include a significant interval in drill hole CGD26-TR-003, which also contained very high-grade copper-gold mineralization over shorter intervals (Photo 1)

  • Hole CGD26-TR-003: 123.60 meters at 0.91% copper, 0.44 g/t of gold and 5.27 g/t of silver from 601.70 meters, including:
    • 71.03 meters at 1.38% copper, 0.52 g/t of gold and 6.73 g/t of silver from 640.32 meters.



Photo 1: High-grade gold, copper and iron-sulfide mineralization in sample TR-003.0437 from the upper breccia domain grading 6.92% copper, 8.88 g/t of gold and 17.25 g/t of silver over 1.13 meters from 674.07 meters in hole CGD26-TR-003.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/3868/324750_8599ff2664613a98_002full.jpg

Assay results from the first nine of eleven completed drill holes also include longer mineralized intervals at similar shallow depths within the breccia and contain shorter sub-intervals at higher grades. The breccia interval in CGD26-TR-008, around 250 meters southwest of CGD26-TR-003 returned:

  • Hole CGD26-TR-008: 381.66 meters at 0.34% copper, 0.29 g/t of gold and 1.07 g/t of silver from 587.85 meters, including:
    • 16.20 meters at 1.04% copper, 0.27 g/t of gold and 1.38 g/t of silver from 729.00 meters; and
    • 41.51 meters at 0.38% copper, 1.23 g/t of gold and 1.78 g/t of silver from 928.00 meters

The primary focus of Ivanhoe Electric's exploration efforts at Gleeson is on delineating the potential continuity and extensions of these mineralized domains. Initial drilling suggests an orientation to the southwest with the mineralization open in several directions. The possibility exists for several mineralized centers at Gleeson.

Mr. Friedland and Mr. Melvin commented: "Our Gleeson Copper-Gold Project in Arizona has suddenly become the Company's highest priority exploration project. These initial drill results are some of the best copper-gold-silver intercepts drilled in the Western United States in the last ten years. These initial discovery results provide us with a glimpse into what we think could become a major new copper-gold-silver district less than 30 miles north of the historic Bisbee District, one of America's most famous and prolific mining districts. Miners at Bisbee extracted over 200 million tonnes of ore from breccia, carbonate and intrusive-hosted mineralization over a 133-year period. Ivanhoe Electric controls a district scale land package that will allow us to explore the full potential of this significant new discovery in this emerging new district, with Gleeson being the focus of what we believe is the best copper-gold-silver exploration project in the United States."

Additional drilling shows visible sulfide mineralization in both breccia and carbonate-replacement domains, with assays expected in the coming weeks

Holes CGD26-TR-008 and CGD26-TR-009 have intersected zones of carbonate replacement mineralization from depths of approximately 1,250 meters (Photos 2, 3 and 4). Assays are in progress with results expected before the end of 2026.

The shallower breccia mineralization domain is also present in holes CGD26-TR-009 (Photo 5) and CGD26-TR-010 from depths of around 600 meters.



Photo 5: CGD26-TR-009 at 698.90 meters, breccia containing pyrite and chalcopyrite, assays pending.

The Gleeson Copper-Gold Project is an emerging copper-gold district north of the historic Bisbee Mining District covering approximately 20,000 acres of mineral rights and 2,000 acres of private surface rights held by Ivanhoe Electric

The Gleeson Copper-Gold Project is located within the historic Courtland-Gleeson Mining District, approximately 28 miles north of Bisbee (Figure 1).

Ivanhoe Electric started acquiring mineral and surface rights in 2024, and currently controls over 19,606 acres of mineral rights and 2,033 acres of private surface rights. Current and planned drilling activities at the Gleeson Copper-Gold Project are occurring entirely on private land controlled by Ivanhoe Electric.



Figure 1. Location map of the Gleeson Copper-Gold Project in southeastern Arizona. 

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/3868/324750_8599ff2664613a98_007full.jpg

The world-famous Bisbee Mining District to the south of Gleeson produced almost continuously from 1880 to 2013, exploiting porphyry and breccia-hosted mineralization intruded into limestones with carbonate-replacement and skarn-type deposits. Over its 133-year life, over 207 million tonnes of ore was mined yielding approximately 8.2 billion pounds of copper, 2.8 million ounces of gold, 105 million ounces of silver, 145,000 tonnes of lead, and 161,000 tonnes of zinc, making it Arizona's largest gold producer, top lead producer, and second-largest silver producer.

Exploration drilling at the Gleeson Copper-Gold Project intersected a significant copper-gold-silver mineralized system from a depth of 600 meters

Complete assay results have been received for the first seven holes, with partial results received for two holes and assays pending for the remaining four, including those in progress (Figure 2, Table 1 and Table 2). Ivanhoe Electric's drilling plan at Gleeson for the remainder of 2026 includes expanding the program to complete a total of 16,000 meters of drilling by the end of 2026. Drilling began in November 2025.



Figure 2. Collar Locations and Drill Traces of Ongoing Ivanhoe Electric Drilling at the Gleeson Copper-Gold Project.

Two mineralized domains have been intersected below a low-angle fault, from a depth of 600 meters (Figures 3 and 4):

  • an upper breccia domain from 600 meters depth that structurally pinches out to the east and broadens to the west. The breccia incorporates fragments of earlier skarn and carbonate-replacement mineralization, intrusions and sediments which are then overprinted by multiple strong copper, gold and silver mineralizing events; and
  • a deeper domain of intrusive-hosted, skarn, and carbonate-replacement mineralization beginning at approximately 1,000 meters depth, with a strong vector from narrow, gold-silver-zinc-lead mineralization in CGD26-TR-003, representing a metal signature further from the source, contrasted by closer to source metal assemblages with copper-gold-silver dominant mineralization in holes CGD25-TR-001 and CGD26-TR-002.

Technical Information and Qualified Person

Disclosures of a scientific or technical nature in this news release have been reviewed and approved by Shawn Vandekerkhove, P.Geo., Vice President, Partnerships and New Opportunities of Ivanhoe Electric. Mr. Vandekerkhove is a "qualified person" as defined in Subpart 1300 of Regulation S-K and a "qualified person" as defined in National Instrument 43-101 Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects. Mr. Vandekerkhove is an employee of Ivanhoe Electric and is not independent of the Company within the meaning of NI 43-101.

Mr. Vandekerkhove verified the sampling and analytical data supporting the reported results. During site visits, he observed drilling, logging, core cutting, sampling and shipment, checked selected collars and drill setups, and examined core from the principal mineralized zones. He checked several dozen randomly selected assays against original laboratory certificates from multiple batches, independently recalculated the reported composites, reviewed their endpoints and reviewed the program's QA/QC results. His review identified no recovery or QA/QC issues that could materially affect the reliability of the reported results. There were no limitations on the verification.

Ivanhoe Electric employs industry best-practice QA/QC and data verification protocols. The diamond drill holes were completed using PQ, HQ, and NQ diameters. The drill core was cut lengthwise into halves using a diamond-bladed saw, with one-half used for the assay sample and the other half retained in core boxes and archived on site. Pulps and rejects are also stored on site for archival purposes. Mineralized zones were generally sampled on 2-meter intervals. Samples were broken at lithological, mineralization, and alteration domain breaks. Each core sample was placed into a bag with a unique numbered sample identification tag. Quality control samples including blanks, duplicates, and certified reference materials were inserted between core samples in a predefined sequence. Then samples were grouped into batches for shipping and laboratory submissions. Chain of custody records are maintained for sample shipments, and the custody is transferred from Ivanhoe Electric to the laboratory preparation facility upon delivery.

Samples were shipped to ALS Laboratories in Tucson, Arizona, for sample preparation and subsequently analyzed at ALS Laboratories in North Vancouver, British Columbia. Samples were analyzed using customary four acid digestion and ICP-MS finish (ME-MS61). A standard gold fire assay package was used to analyze for gold (Au-ICP21). ME-OG62 was used to analyze for overlimit Cu, Ag, Pb, and Zn; some Ag were further analyzed using gravimetric finish (Ag-GRA21) depending on silver concentrations. ALS Laboratories in North Vancouver, British Columbia, is an independent laboratory accredited to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 by the Standards Council of Canada for the analytical methods performed.

Qualification milestones expand device options for mission-critical space applications

CHANDLER, Ariz., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) is strengthening its portfolio of high-reliability aerospace and defense solutions with new spaceflight qualifications for its radiation-tolerant (RT) PolarFire® FPGA and SoC families. The RT PolarFire FPGA RTPF500ZT has achieved Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Qualified Manufacturers List (QML) Class V qualification, the highest qualification standard for space microelectronics. Additionally, the RT PolarFire SoC FPGA RTPFS460ZT has completed QML Class Q and MIL-STD-883 Class B qualifications. These milestones provide developers with flight-ready components for systems with stringent reliability requirements.

“As space applications demand greater onboard processing capability within increasingly constrained SWaP budgets, developers need technologies that maximize performance without increasing power consumption or thermal complexity,” said Shakeel Peera, corporate vice president of Microchip’s FPGA business unit. “Our RT PolarFire portfolio combines a power-efficient, radiation-tolerant architecture designed to be immune to radiation-induced upsets and defense-grade security to help developers reduce system power, simplify thermal management and build highly integrated, mission-critical space systems.”

 The majority of SRAM-based FPGAs typically require configuration scrubbing to correct radiation-induced upsets which can remain undetected between scrubbing cycles and increase power consumption. RT PolarFire devices use configuration technology designed to eliminate configuration Single-Event Upset (SEU) concerns. The devices’ power-efficient operation helps address the thermal limits of space platforms, and defense-grade security helps protect mission-critical systems while reducing system complexity. With high reliability and radiation tolerance, RT PolarFire devices are designed for aerospace and defense applications, from satellite payloads and constellations to human-rated spacecraft and deep-space missions.

The flight proven QML-V qualified RTPF500ZT PolarFire FPGA features Single-Event Latch-Up (SEL) radiation performance and in-flight programmability for mission-critical space applications requiring high reliability for demanding missions. The RTPFS460ZT PolarFire SoC FPGA combines programmable logic with an integrated Microprocessor Subsystem (MSS) featuring 64-bit RISC-V® processor cores and is qualified to MIL-STD-883 Class B and QML Class Q. Available development kits, together with a common RT PolarFire architecture and tool flow help streamline evaluation, prototyping and flight-system development.

MIL-STD-883 and QML qualification establish testing, manufacturing and quality requirements for microelectronic devices used in high-reliability aerospace and defense applications. MIL-STD-883 defines uniform environmental, mechanical and electrical test methods, while QML Class V under MIL-PRF-38535 establishes space-level quality and reliability assurance requirements. Together, these requirements help customers address stringent reliability and mission assurance needs for critical space applications. Visit the website to learn more about Microchip’s full portfolio of radiation-tolerant FPGAs.

Development Tools
The RTPFS460ZT development kit enables evaluation and prototyping of the RT PolarFire SoC FPGA, and both devices are supported by Microchip’s Libero® SoC Design Suite for overall design and development and the Mi-V® ecosystem for RISC-V development. Together, these resources provide a cohesive environment to evaluate the architecture, validate designs and reuse engineering work as programs progress toward flight hardware.
